title: Pennsylvania National Guard Hurricane Harvey support wrap-up
description:
Two-hundred and three Pennsylvania National Guard members provided air and ground support to Texas in response to Hurricane Harvey, which devastated the state and caused catastrophic damage.

Six Pennsylvania Air National Guard and 197 Pennsylvania Army National Guardsmen on State Active Duty status, along with 2 CH-47 Chinook helicopters and 7 fuel trucks, all arrived to Texas within 72 hours of being activated and conducted missions in support of domestic operations between Austin and Houston, Texas from Aug. 28 to Sept. 7.

Pennsylvania National Guard units involved include the 213th Personnel Company, 2-104th Cavalry Regiment, 228th Transportation Battalion, 721st Transportation Company, 108th Medical Company, 252nd Quartermaster Company, 1-109th Field Artillery, 1067th Transportation Company, 628th Support Battalion, 131st Transportation Company, 2-104th General Support Aviation Battalion, and Joint Force Headquarters, Pennsylvania National Guard.

transcript.text: - [Reporter] 203 Pennsylvania National Guard members
provided air and ground support to Texas
in response to Hurricane Harvey,
which devastated the state and caused catastrophic damage.
The hurricane made landfall in Texas
as a category four storm on August 28th.
Six Pennsylvania National Guard airmen
provided joint incident site communications capabilities
from August 28th to September seventh.
10 Pennsylvania National Guard soldiers
and two CH-47 Chinook helicopters provided aviation support,
transporting personnel and equipment between Austin
and Houston, Texas,
in support of domestic operations
from September second to 11th.
165 soldiers provided general aviation maintenance support
to assist with relief efforts from September 4th to 11th.
These soldiers also assisted Texas farmers
by loading 800-pound hay bales into a CH-47 Chinook
to deliver to stranded cattle and horses
cut off from food following Hurricane Harvey.
10 soldiers provided logistical support
and an additional 12 soldiers provided
convoy supply support from September 4th to 11th.
All Pennsylvania National Guard soldiers, airmen,
and equipment returned safely to Pennsylvania
following the completion of their missions.
21 first went on to conduct a follow-on mission
from Texas to Florida in support of Hurricane Irma.
